answer: If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there and got a fine.
other_correct: If I'd seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there and got a fine.
If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there and (wouldn't have) gotten a fine.
If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there or got a fine.
If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there, so I wouldn't have got a fine.
If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have got a fine.
instruction_problem: Two results (parked / got a fine) and the instruction does not say whether one or both must go into the result clause, so many answers are possible; 'and got a fine' after a negative clause reads oddly ('or got' / 'wouldn't have got').

answer: My sister advised me to see a doctor about my cough.
other_correct: My sister urged me to see a doctor about my cough.
My sister recommended that I (should) see a doctor about my cough.
My sister recommended seeing a doctor about my cough.
My sister suggested that I (should) see a doctor about my cough.
My sister told me (that) I really should see a doctor about my cough.
My sister advised me to go to the doctor about my cough.
instruction_problem: 'Say what my sister did' is vague: it does not signal that a reporting verb (advise/urge) is wanted, so 'told me I should...' is equally valid; many correct answers to accept.

answer: We visited a museum which has old cars.
other_correct: We visited a museum which had old cars.
We visited a museum, which has old cars.

sense_problem: 'a museum which has old cars' is slightly unnatural; 'a museum with old cars' / 'a car museum' is what a native would say.

answer: The app which helps me learn new words is free.
other_correct: The app, which helps me learn new words, is free.
The app which is free helps me learn new words.
The app, which is free, helps me learn new words.
instruction_problem: Two different embeddings are correct (which helps... is free / which is free helps...), plus comma vs no-comma variants; the instruction does not say which sentence becomes the clause.
level_problem: Embedding a relative clause in the middle of the sentence is harder than A2.2 end-position joining.

sense_problem: Solvable purely by meaning (general knowledge); the who/which grammar is never tested, since each ending fits only one beginning logically. 'A tourist is someone who travels for fun' is a loose definition.

answer: I have decided to go home early.
other_correct: I've decided to go home early.
I decided to go home early.
I've decided I will go home early.
I've decided that I'll go home early.
instruction_problem: 'Make a sentence with decide' is unclear: tense of 'decide' is not given, and it is not explained that 'will' (spontaneous decision) should become 'decide to'; 'I will decide to go home early' would follow the instruction literally but is wrong.
